Subject: RE: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — initial discovery + next tests

Alex — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Summary from call:
- Primary goal: confirm latency and throughput profile for your inference-heavy chat pipeline (Gen-2 model family).
- Success criteria you mentioned: p95 latency under ~300ms for single-request flows and sustained tokens/sec that meet your traffic peaks.
- Concern: consistency at p99 during traffic spikes & cold cache behavior.

2) Proposed A/B test (what we'd like you to run or let BenchOps run):
- Compare Redwood hosted endpoint vs your current hyperscaler endpoint (Bedrock) and a quantized variant where possible.
- Workloads: short interactive requests (avg 80 tokens), and bulk generation (avg 800 tokens).
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec (aggregate and per-worker), error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, tail latencies during a 10-minute sustained run at target RPS.
- Cache state: please capture cold-start, warm-cache (after steady traffic), and warm-KV-cache (if you can run a prefix reuse scenario).

3) Logistics & artifacts:
- If you want, we can run the A/B harness from our infra and share the CSVs. Otherwise, BenchOps (cc'd) can run on your behalf.
- Attachment: small test harness + configuration (redwood_abtest_template.sh).

4) Next steps:
- Can BenchOps/Nick confirm whether they can run the 10-min sustained run by end of week? If not, we can schedule Redwood to run it Monday.
- I'll follow up with a proposed canary plan and success gates once we have results.

Thanks — looking forward to the numbers.

--

Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscalers — A/B test results (prelim)

Marissa / Alex — attaching the preliminary CSV and quick summary from the run we executed yesterday. We followed the harness and ran: cold-start batch, warm-cache steady state (10 min at 100rps), and a KV-prefill scenario for prefix reuse. Attachments: redwood_globex_abtest_results_20260902.csv, p99_latency_report_20260902.pdf

Quick summary (aggregated):
- Redwood (hosted, default runtime): p50 85ms, p95 182ms, p99 430ms, tokens/sec (sustained) 2,200 tps
- Redwood (with KV caching + quantized FP16): p50 74ms, p95 150ms, p99 360ms, tokens/sec 2,750 tps (≈ +25%)
- Bedrock (reference hyperscaler config): p50 120ms, p95 240ms, p99 610ms, tokens/sec 1,800 tps
- Observations: Redwood shows noticeably better tail latencies (p99) and higher tokens/sec in the warm-KV-cache case. Bedrock had higher variance under sustained 10-min runs — p99 spiked during queuing events.

Test notes / caveats:
- Model parity: we used the same base model family; Bedrock ran a managed variant with slightly different quantization. We flagged that for your teams; see CSV details.
- Cold-starts were comparable but converged after ~60s of traffic.
- All runs collected GPU utilization and request traces; full traces are available in the Drive link.

If you want a deeper breakdown (per-request histograms, kernel-level timings), we can generate that overnight.

— BenchOps Team

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the numbers — useful. A few clarifying questions before we move to a canary:

1) Can you confirm the exact harness version and whether the Redwood runs included kernel-level optimizations + continuous batching? We want to make sure we're comparing apples-to-apples.
2) For the KV caching scenario: what's the hit rate during the 10-min run and how did you pre-populate the cache?
3) Bedrock's managed quantization is something we can't change; how should we interpret the quantized Redwood result vs their managed variant?

Proposed next test: a sustained 30-minute run at 100rps (gradually ramping) to validate long tail behavior. Also want to run a synthetic spike (2x traffic for 2 minutes) to validate graceful degradation.

If Redwood can run the 30-min test from your side (and include kernel timings), that would be ideal. Otherwise we'll coordinate another BenchOps run.

— Alex

Alex — great questions. Quick replies and next steps below, plus a proposed canary window.

1) Harness & runtime details: Redwood runs included our production runtime with continuous batching and kernel selection enabled. We ran the same model graph and used our FP16 quantization path for the quantized runs. I'll attach the runtime config and kernel timing extract (see attached CSV).

2) KV caching: hit rate averaged ~68% during the 10-min run; we prefilled using a sampled prefix set representative of your traffic (BenchOps helped with the sampling).

3) Comparison approach: treat the managed hyperscaler quantization as a different configuration. The most actionable comparison is the warm-cache p95/p99 and sustained tokens/sec under your target load — that's where Redwood shows measurable advantages. We'll include a footnote in the report about the managed quantization differences.

Proposed canary plan (high level):
- Window: Sep 10–12 (72 hours)
- Tests: 30-min sustained run at 100rps, a 2-minute 2x spike, and 1-hour low-latency interactive sampling.
- Success gates: p95 < 250ms, sustained tokens/sec > 2,000, error rate < 0.5%, no unhandled p99 spikes > 800ms.
- Rollback: auto-failover to existing Bedrock endpoint + 30-min cooldown if any gate breaches.

Commercials & paperwork: I'll have Rishi/Monica send a proposed POC quote today. I can also generate a short DocuSign for the POC terms if you want to fast-track legal. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sandbox/ABC123-redwood-globex-poc

Can you confirm: a) the canary window works for your team, and b) who will be the primary contact on your side for execution?

If yes, we'll lock dates and start the procurement steps.

Thanks — talk soon.
